title: Encoding or encryption?
instruction: A rule every program knows, or a lock that only someone has the key to?

items.text: The letter A is stored as 65
items.why: Every computer knows the character table. Nothing is secret.
The PNG format is public. Any image viewer can open it.

items.text: A chat message only the recipient can read
items.why: The message is locked with a key only the recipient has. That's encryption.

items.text: A pixel as three numbers: red, green, blue
items.why: A public rule for writing a colour as numbers.

items.text: The padlock and https in your browser
items.why: The connection to the website is encrypted, so nobody on the way can read it.
MP3 is a public format. Any player can play it.

items.text: A Caesar cipher with a key of 3
items.why: Without the key (a shift of 3) you can't read the message. It's a cipher, if a weak one.

debrief: Encoding is a public rule for writing data as numbers. Every program knows it. Encryption locks the data, and only someone with the key can read it.
